world.description: a pencil logistics and supply network

world.label: Pencil Supply Network
world.summary: Specialists turn renewable timber and mined graphite into pencils that move through a shop to customers.

actions.description: Grow one log's worth of timber in the managed forest.
Harvest one log from the managed forest into the forester's stock.
Take one log from the forester's stock and make one pencil slat in the sawmill worker's stock.
Add one unit of graphite ore to the graphite seam.
Mine one unit of ore from the graphite seam into the miner's stock.
Take one unit of ore from the miner's stock and make one graphite lead in the graphite works operator's stock.
Take one slat from the sawmill worker and one graphite lead from the graphite works operator to assemble one pencil in the pencil maker's stock.
Carry one pencil from the pencil maker to the pencil shop.
Sell one pencil from the shop's stock to a customer.

mechanics.rationale: A forester can grow one log into the managed forest; this changes only the forest's represented log stock.

checks.label: The forester grows and harvests timber
The managed forest is at the supply network

limits: This action grows exactly one log in the selected managed forest; it does not harvest timber.
tests: The forester can add one log to the managed forest.
A worker with a different role cannot regrow timber.
semantic_bindings: forest is the forest action field
forest logs are represented by components.stock.logs

mechanics.rationale: Harvesting transfers one represented log from the managed forest to the forester's stock.

checks.label: The forester grows and harvests timber
The managed forest has a log
The forester and managed forest are at the supply network
The selected forest is at the supply network

limits: Harvest requires at least one forest log and moves exactly one log into the forester's stock.
tests: With a log in the forest, harvesting reduces forest stock by one and adds one to the forester.
Harvesting is refused when the forest has no logs.
semantic_bindings: forest is the forest action field

mechanics.rationale: The sawmill worker consumes one log from the named source and produces one slat in its own stock.

checks.label: The worker turns logs into pencil slats
The forester has a log
The named source is the forester

limits: Only a forester with at least one log can supply this action; one log makes one slat.
tests: A sawmill worker with a forester source holding one log consumes it and gains one slat.
The action is refused if the source has no logs or is not a forester.
semantic_bindings: source is the source action field
logs and slats are represented by components.stock.logs and components.stock.slats

mechanics.rationale: The graphite miner replenishes one unit of represented ore in the named seam, as described by the action.

checks.label: The miner mines graphite ore
The graphite seam is at the supply network

limits: This action adds exactly one ore unit to the selected seam; it does not mine ore into a worker's stock.
tests: The graphite miner can add one ore unit to the graphite seam.
A worker with a different role cannot replenish graphite.
semantic_bindings: seam is the seam action field

mechanics.rationale: Mining transfers one represented ore unit from the named seam to the miner's stock.

checks.label: The miner mines graphite ore
The graphite seam has ore
The miner and graphite seam are at the supply network
The selected seam is at the supply network

limits: Mining requires at least one ore unit in the seam and moves exactly one unit to the miner.
tests: With ore available, mining reduces seam stock by one and adds one to the miner.
Mining is refused when the seam has no ore.
semantic_bindings: seam is the seam action field

mechanics.rationale: The graphite works operator consumes one ore unit from the named source and produces one lead in its own stock.

checks.label: The operator processes ore into graphite leads
The miner has ore
The named source is the graphite miner

limits: Only a graphite miner with at least one ore unit can supply this action; one ore makes one lead.
tests: A graphite works operator can consume one miner ore and gain one lead.
The action is refused if the source has no ore or is not the graphite miner.
semantic_bindings: source is the source action field
ore and leads are components.stock.graphite_ore and components.stock.graphite_leads

mechanics.rationale: The pencil maker consumes one slat and one graphite lead from the named sources and adds one pencil to its stock.

checks.label: The worker assembles pencil parts
The sawmill worker has a slat
The slat source is the sawmill worker
The graphite works operator has a lead
The lead source is the graphite works operator

limits: Assembly requires one slat from a sawmill worker and one lead from a graphite works operator.
tests: With both parts available from the matching sources, assembly consumes one of each and adds one pencil.
Assembly is refused if either part is missing or either source has the wrong role.
semantic_bindings: slat_source and lead_source are the respective action fields
slats, leads, and pencils are represented by components.stock.slats, components.stock.graphite_leads, and components.stock.pencils

mechanics.rationale: The represented delivery transfers one pencil from the named pencil maker's stock to the named shop's stock.

checks.label: The worker moves pencils between businesses
The pencil maker has a pencil
The named source is the pencil maker
The named destination is the pencil shop

limits: Delivery moves exactly one pencil and requires a pencil maker source holding a pencil and a pencil shop destination.
tests: A carrier can transfer one available pencil from the pencil maker to the pencil shop.
Delivery is refused if the source has no pencils or the destination is not the pencil shop.
semantic_bindings: source and to are the action fields for the pencil maker and shop

mechanics.rationale: Selling consumes one pencil from the shop's stock; no customer inventory, payment, or order state is represented.

checks.label: The shop sells pencils to customers
The shop has a pencil
The customer is at the supply network
The shop is at the supply network

limits: Selling removes one pencil from shop stock; customer demand, possession, and payment cannot be represented with the available state.
tests: With a pencil in stock and a customer at the supply network, the shop's pencil count decreases by one.
Selling is refused when the shop has no pencils or the customer is elsewhere.
semantic_bindings: customer is the customer action field
shop pencils are represented by components.stock.pencils

processes.rationale: Managed forests are renewable timber sources; restoring one log per round keeps raw timber available without making processed goods.
The graphite seam is a raw-material source; replenishing one ore unit per round keeps graphite available without making processed goods.

readout.title: How goods moved through the chain
readout.summary: The forester supplied logs, the sawmill made slats, and the graphite miner and graphite works supplied graphite leads. The pencil maker combined slats and leads into pencils, the carrier brought them to the pencil shop, and the shop sold them repeatedly.

mechanisms.name: Goods made from other goods
mechanisms.explanation: The graphite works refined ore into graphite leads and the sawmill made slats from logs. The pencil maker used leads and slats to assemble pencils.

mechanisms.name: Goods carried to the next step
mechanisms.explanation: The forester and graphite miner moved raw materials into their stocks, and the carrier moved pencils from the pencil maker to the pencil shop.

mechanisms.name: Demand reached and met
mechanisms.explanation: The pencil shop sold a pencil from its stock, showing finished pencils reached the shop and were taken there.

mechanisms.name: Work held up
mechanisms.missing_reason: No recorded event shows work held up while waiting for needed goods.
